claims.quote: Rapid intercourse, from which the previous civilisation had hoped so much, had ended by defeating itself. What was the good of going to Pekin when it was just like Shrewsbury?
claims.description: Fast global travel and technology make the whole earth uniform, so travel loses its point.

claims.quote: She touched the isolation knob, so that no one else could speak to her.
claims.description: A communication switch lets a person block all incoming calls and messages in a global network.

claims.quote: A faint blue light shot across it, darkening to purple, and presently she could see the image of her son, who lived on the other side of the earth, and he could see her.
claims.description: A handheld screen provides live two-way video calls across the globe.

claims.quote: The clumsy system of public gatherings had been long since abandoned; neither Vashti nor her audience stirred from their rooms. Seated in her arm-chair she spoke, while they in their arm-chairs heard her, fairly well, and saw her, fairly well.
claims.description: Lectures and meetings take place remotely through audio-video links, replacing public gatherings.

claims.quote: There were buttons and switches everywhere—buttons to call for food, for music, for clothing.
claims.description: A fully automated room delivers food, music, clothing, baths, and literature on demand at the press of a button.

claims.quote: Immediately an enormous apparatus fell on to her out of the ceiling, a thermometer was automatically inserted between her lips, a stethoscope was automatically laid upon her heart.
claims.description: Automated remote medical diagnosis and treatment by machine, summoned by telegraph, with medicine projected into the mouth.

claims.quote: Beneath those corridors of shining tiles were rooms, tier below tier, reaching far into the earth, and in each room there sat a human being, eating, or sleeping, or producing ideas.
claims.description: Humanity lives in isolated individual underground cells in a vast hive-like network.

claims.quote: The surface of the earth is only dust and mud, no life remains on it, and you would need a respirator, or the cold of the outer air would kill you. One dies immediately in the outer air.
claims.description: The earth's surface becomes uninhabitable, with humans living underground and needing respirators to go outside.

claims.quote: Men made it, do not forget that. Great men, but men. The Machine is much, but it is not everything.
claims.description: A single global Machine governs all human needs and life, and people come to worship it and treat its Book as sacred.

claims.quote: Each infant was examined at birth, and all who promised undue strength were destroyed.
claims.description: Newborns judged physically too strong are killed to keep the population adapted to the Machine.

claims.quote: Parents, duties of," said the book of the Machine, "cease at the moment of birth.
claims.description: Children are raised in public nurseries and parental duties end at birth; reproduction requires committee approval.

claims.quote: Homelessness means death. The victim is exposed to the air, which kills him.
claims.description: Punishment of banishment to the deadly outer air is imposed by a central Committee.

claims.quote: Racing aeroplanes had been built for the purpose, capable of enormous speed, and steered by the greatest intellects of the epoch.
claims.description: Aeroplanes race around the globe westward to try to keep pace with or outstrip the sun.

claims.quote: Vessel after vessel would rise from the vomitories of Rye or of Christchurch (I use the antique names), would sail into the crowded sky, and would draw up at the wharves of the south—empty.
claims.description: A worldwide network of air-ships on fixed schedules crosses the sky between continents in about two days.

claims.quote: The forests had been destroyed during the literature epoch for the purpose of making newspaper-pulp
claims.description: Himalayan forests are cleared for newspaper pulp, leaving diminished rivers and ruined cities.

claims.quote: We say 'space is annihilated,' but we have annihilated not space, but the sense thereof. We have lost a part of ourselves.
claims.description: Technology causes humans to lose the physical sense of space and distance.

claims.quote: There was the hot-bath button, by pressure of which a basin of (imitation) marble rose out of the floor, filled to the brim with a warm deodorised liquid.
claims.description: Rooms contain automated retractable bathing apparatus and artificial surroundings.

claims.quote: I climbed with my respirator and my hygienic clothes and my dietetic tabloids!
claims.description: Respirators and compressed dietary tablets enable a person to survive outside the underground city.

claims.quote: Then she fed, talked to many friends, had a bath, talked again, and summoned her bed.
claims.description: Furniture such as beds is summoned by machinery, with identical standardised beds worldwide.
